profile.constituencyprofile_Text: The Hindupur Constituency is on the western side of Sri Sathya Sai District, Puttaparthi, Andhra Pradesh, bordering Karnataka. It appears that the town was at first founded by one Sri Hindu Rao by the name Siddhoji, the father of Morarji Rao of Gooty and thus it is named after him. Hindupur is a Mandal in Sri Sathya Sai District of Andhra Pradesh State, India. It belongs to the Rayalaseema region. It is located 72 KM towards the western side of the district headquarters Sri Sathya Sai District, Puttaparthi. 562 KM from the State capital Amaravathi.  Hindupur Constituency is with a spanning an area of 567.15 sq.km. Hindupur Constituency formed with Hindupur (Rural & Urban), Lepakshi, Chilamathur Mandals, and it is part of the Hindupur parliament constituency in the Sri Sathya Sai District of Andhra Pradesh. The Hindupur Constituency is known for Industrial hub, Power loom and Silk industry. Hindupur Constituency stands for their significant contributions to the industrial, Sericulture, construction, education, commerce, and service sectors. These unique advantages position the constituency to achieve an ambitious annual growth target of 15% across all key sectors. Lepakshi and Chilamathur Mandals in Hindupur Constituency have a rich historical legacy. The constituency including, 40 Gram Panchayats & 178 habitations are strategically located, connecting   to International Airport of Devanahalli at 80 Km., from Bengaluru of Karnataka state. It is an important local pilgrimage centre with a number of temples in and around the segment, including Sri Peta Venkata Ramana Swamy Temple, Sree Vasavi Kanyaka Parameswari  vari Temple, Guddam Sri Ranganath Swamy Temple, Sugur Sri Anjaneya  Swamy Temple in Hindupur town, and the historical  famous Sri Veerabhadra Swamy Temple @ Lepakshi.
profile.geography: Hindupur Assembly Constituency is strategically located in Sri Sathya Sai District within the Rayalaseema Region. The constituency is situated in a semi-arid region with a relatively flat terrain. It is part of the Deccan Plateau, characterized by rocky outcrops and dry land agriculture. The region has a mix of red loamy soil (74%) and black cotton soil (26%), supporting a variety of crops. Agriculture, Horticulture and Sericulture are key activities, with 40,043 hectares of cultivable land, 5,940 tube wells, covering 3,446 hectares.
profile.populationDesc: Hindupur has a total population of 3,00,116, with 49.52% residing in rural areas and 50.48% in urban areas. The constituency has 69,570 households, with a sex ratio of 978 females per 1,000 males. The literacy rate stands at 65.89%.
profile.administrationDesc: Hindupur Constituency is one of the six assembly constituencies in Sri Satya Sai  District. It includes 1) Hindupur Mandal 2)Lepakshi Mandal 3) Chilamathur Mandals and also it has Hindupur municipality.
profile.educationHealthcareDesc: Hindupur Constituency Educational infrastructure comprises 59 Government high schools, 3 Residential Schools, one Jawahar Navodaya vidyalaya at Lepakshi, 19 junior colleges, and four-degree college, I Polytechnic college for girls, 3 ITIs and 1 Engineering College. Social infrastructure includes one Government Head quarter hospital, seven primary health centers (PHCs), and 86 sub-centers, 2 ESI, 5 Urban PHCs, 3 Ayurvedic, 1 Homeo and 1 Unani hospital.
profile.culturalheritageDesc: Lepakshi: A historic village 15 km east of Hindupur. It is renowned for its Vijayanagar-era architecture, particularly the Veerabhadra Temple, featuring intricate sculptures and frescoes. The name derives from the Telugu phrase Le Pakshi ("Rise, Bird"), linked to the Ramayana. Key attractions include the Natya and Ardha Mandapas, and the unfinished Kalyana Mandapa, believed to depict Shiva and Parvati’s wedding.

economy_text.economy_Text:
Hindupur’s Gross Constituency Domestic Product (GCDP) is projected to grow from ₹9,674 crores in 2023–24 to ₹20,769 crores by 2028–29, achieving a nominal CAGR of 15%. 

The economy will remain industry-led (51.9% GVA), with services (37%) and agriculture (11.4%) deepening diversification. 

Key sub-sectors include horticulture, sericulture, and livestock in agriculture; MSME clusters (textiles, engineering, chemicals), large-scale manufacturing and APIIC industrial parks in industry; and real estate, IT, tourism (Lepakshi’s UNESCO status) and healthcare in services. 

Growth drivers encompass industrial land development, connectivity to Bengaluru airport and NH corridors, renewable energy, skill hubs and digital governance. 

MSME expansion, textile modernization, and work-from-home IT policies will boost employment, particularly for women and youth, while climate-smart irrigation, cold chains, and green estates ensure sustainability. 

By 2029, Hindupur aims to emerge as an investment-friendly, employment-rich model constituency with robust industrial, logistics, and tourism infrastructure, aligned with the Swarna Andhra @2047 vision.
economy_text.gcdP_Growth_Text: Hindupur is witnessing steady economic momentum with a targeted 15% annual GCDP growth rate across key sectors like real estate, industrial infrastructure, livestock, skilling and employment. This growth trajectory aligns with the long-term vision of making the constituency a vibrant rural and economic hub by 2047
